To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

children adapt to the new school environment by means of security-seeking behavior and behavioral inhibition and that children who have more behavioral and emotional problems before entry to school are more likely to show these behaviors in the first months of school.

children adapt to kindergarten by means of security-seeking and inhibition, that children with behavioral, emotional, or family problems have more problems in adapting, and that children in regular classes adapt faster than children in special classes, especially in the area of emotional security.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the process of adaptation after school entry, with special attention to the regulation of emotional security.
the question of how children adapt to school.
the development of children's emotional security and the role of the teacher and the family in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the more children are insecure in their attachment to the teacher, the more they are inhibited in their approach to her and the more problems they have in the first 3 months at school, especially if they have problems in other areas of life as well.

children in regular classes show less behavioral inhibition and security seeking than children in special classes, but both groups adapt quickly to their new school environment and that the process of adaptation can be described as a process of emotional security.

emotional security and behavioral inhibition are important factors in the adaptation process of young children in the first months after entry to school and that they are related to behavioral problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
children adapt to the school environment by means of behavioral inhibition, and that this process is mediated by emotional security seeking, which is in turn related to recent stress in the family.
children adapt to kindergarten by seeking emotional security and by inhibiting their behavior in order to achieve this goal.
children from special kindergarten classes are more emotionally insecure and more variable than children in regular classes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
teachers should pay attention to the early adaptation process, as it is an important determinant of children's behavior problems later on.
the emotional security of young children is a dynamic process.
the process of adaptation after school entry is a process of obtaining security.
